title: The Architecture of Desire: Gardening the Mind and Mentally Exerted Fasting
summary: Preparing for a prophet-led worldwide fast, President Hughes unpacks a general conference teaching by President Dallin H. Oaks: desires dictate priorities, shape choices, and determine destiny. He asserts that missionaries are not their thoughts, but rather the inspectors of them, using the metaphor of a gardener weeding out fear and negativity. Quoting Brigham Young on the mystery of mind control, he connects thought management directly to spiritual endurance. Finally, he outlines guidelines for the upcoming fast, urging missionaries to stay hydrated and practice 'mental exertion' rather than simply skipping meals.
